comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited restaurant 40 meters away in the same NCD-Lakeside Village zoning district, approved in 2019 via Health Department referral for a simple limited restaurant use—the closest match to the concept's limited cooking designation.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral imposed an 11 p.m. closing condition citing Planning Code Section 716, showing that even a principally permitted limited restaurant can carry an hours restriction when routed through Health rather than approved by right at the building permit stage.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Full-service restaurant with ABC Type 41 beer-and-wine license immediately adjacent (12 meters away, 2642 Ocean Ave) in identical zoning, approved January 2023—the most recent decision on this block and directly next door to the subject site.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This ABC agency referral was approved in 19 days with no conditions, citing restaurant use as permitted under Planning Code Section 727. The speed and lack of conditions reflect routine treatment of restaurant continuation in this corridor, though formula retail was explicitly noted as not permitted.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Full-service restaurant (Lucho's) with ABC Type 41 at 2675 Ocean Ave (53 meters away), same zoning district, approved May 2021 as a continuation with beer-and-wine service—demonstrates recent approval pattern for alcohol-serving restaurants on this block.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 14 days citing Planning Code Sections 710 and 202.2(a) eating/drinking use conditions. The reference to Section 202.2(a) signals that even routine approvals invoke the standard restaurant operating conditions (trash, noise, queuing) in NCD districts.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: The only use decision (Conditional Use Authorization) found among the candidates, approved in 1988 at 2642–2646 Ocean Ave (12 meters away, same parcel as the 2023 ABC referral) to expand a small fast-food restaurant into a large fast-food restaurant in the then-NC-1 district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A CUA was required 36 years ago to create a large fast-food restaurant at this exact neighboring address. No conditions were extracted, and the use has continued through multiple ownership changes since. This signals that once a restaurant use is established via CUA or by right, changes of ownership are handled as routine agency referrals.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Full-service restaurant (Lucho's) at 2675 Ocean Ave (53 meters), approved September 2018 via Health referral for continuation of use, same NCD-Lakeside Village zoning—shows the corridor's stable restaurant character and referral process.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in one day, citing Planning Code Sections 710 and 202.2(a). The one-day turnaround for a Health Department sign-off underscores that established restaurant uses on Ocean Avenue face minimal Planning review when there is no change of use or expansion.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant (My Cup of Tea) at 2660 Ocean Ave (36 meters away), approved November 2017 as a change-of-ownership continuation in NCD-Lakeside Village zoning, no alcohol, demonstrating treatment of non-alcohol restaurant transitions.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 17 days with no extracted conditions, described as 'continuation of existing use, change of ownership only.' This confirms that non-alcohol restaurants moving into established restaurant spaces receive swift, unconditioned approvals on this corridor.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant (Ocean Thai) at 2545 Ocean Ave (124 meters), approved February 2018 as continuation of a restaurant use established in 2002, same NCD-Lakeside Village zoning, illustrating long-term restaurant precedent along the broader Ocean Avenue corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in two days, explicitly referencing the original 2002 permit (MB0200855). The multi-decade continuity of restaurant uses on Ocean Avenue and the speed of change-of-ownership approvals demonstrate Planning's comfort with the restaurant corridor character.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for a California Seller's Permit with the Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) to collect sales tax on food and beverage sales.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online using the EIN. The permit is free and often issued the same day. CDTFA may request a security deposit depending on projected taxable sales.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Submit architectural plans for tenant improvements to the San Francisco Department of Building Inspection for a building permit, including DBI plan check, Planning zoning review (Section 175 referral), Public Health plan check, and any required plumbing, mechanical, and electrical permits pulled by…
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire a California-licensed architect experienced with San Francisco restaurant build-outs to prepare a stamped plan set showing the kitchen layout, hood and fire suppression system, three-compartment sink, hand-washing sinks, ADA-compliant restrooms, grease interceptor location, and occupant load calculation. Submit the plans to DBI with a Building Permit Application (BPA) designating 'health' and 'planning' as routing stations. In the cover letter reference the CUA case number (if applicable) and confirm that the proposed use is a restaurant with limited cooking. Request simultaneous DPH and Planning review to avoid serial delays. Budget 14–120 days for plan review depending on completeness and the number of correction rounds.

timeline_cost.notes: The day and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization and the Health Permit to Operate, the two approvals in the entitlement path, and reflect the time to approval when those approvals are granted (not the time to a denial or withdrawal). The CUA timeline is estimated at 120–300 days from filing to Planning Commission hearing and final approval based on typical San Francisco hearing timelines for neighborhood commercial conditional use cases; the single comparable CUA in the candidate set (1988.272C at 2642 Ocean Ave) took 45 days in 1988, but that pre-dates current environmental review, neighborhood notification, and hearing-scheduling procedures. The health permit takes 14–45 days after plan check is complete and prerequisites are met. The cost range includes the CUA filing fee (approximately $3,100 for a use decision without construction in 2024, CPI-adjusted annually per the Planning fee schedule), the health permit application fee ($470 for FY 2026–27), and the plan-check fee ($828–$2,207 for a new restaurant depending on complexity, FY 2026–27 schedule). Total estimated government fees for the two approvals are $4,400–$5,700. Building permit fees ($800–$15,000) are not included because the building row has insufficient-information status, but they will add materially once the change-of-use determination is made. State and federal registrations (EIN, Secretary of State, seller's permit) add $70–$150 and take 1–10 days but are prerequisites, not approvals in the entitlement path.
timeline_cost.path: Conditional Use Authorization (Planning Code § 303); Health permit to operate
timeline_cost.verification_note: Records support health permit timing (14-45 days), health permit fee ($470), and plan-check fees ($828-$2,207 stated, though record shows upper bound of $2,500); no CUA catalog entry cited, no support for CUA timeline or fees.

status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.

records_summary: The records show 2650 Ocean Ave is in the NCD-Lakeside Village zoning district, where a restaurant on the first story is principally permitted. The site is also within the Family and Senior Housing Opportunity Special Use District. No prior applications or permits appear on file at this exact address or parcel (7223/004). The immediate block is an established restaurant corridor: within 500 feet there are 6 registered food/drink businesses and 3 active ABC Type 41 licenses (beer-and-wine restaurants). The surrounding Ocean Avenue addresses show a 30-year pattern of restaurant approvals—mostly change-of-ownership referrals—with no use decisions denied within 1,000 feet in the available records.
